paragraphs: The Cinema Message, posted by Mia. Teacher Kim wants the Explorers to see a film together. It will be our trip for this month. On Monday, she asked me to call the town cinema. Nobody answered the phone, but I heard a recorded message. I wrote it down with a pen and a notebook. It was short, but it had many numbers. Here is the message.

"Hello, and thank you for calling the town cinema. We are open every day from ten o'clock in the morning until ten o'clock at night. The ticket office closes at lunchtime, from twelve o'clock to one o'clock. This week, we have three films. At eleven o'clock, we show a film about the sea. It is a relaxing film for everyone. At two o'clock, we show a film about robots. At five o'clock, we show a film about a family on a ski holiday.

An adult ticket costs two hundred baht. A child ticket costs one hundred baht. The price is the same on every day of the week. Children under six enter for free, but they must sit with an adult. Each ticket has a seat number on it. Please come ten minutes before the film, because the door closes when the film begins. Please turn off your phone in the film. Do not bring food into the room. You can buy a snack in the small shop.

If you have a big group, please call again. Call between two o'clock and four o'clock. Ask for the group ticket office. Our group number is five, five, two, nine, one. The cinema is next to the town library. Thank you, and enjoy the film."

I called the group number at three o'clock. A woman answered the phone. I said, "We are a school club." "Certainly," she said. "Twenty children can come on Saturday." I told Teacher Kim the news, and she smiled. We chose the film about the sea, because Leo loves fish. Leo is already very excited. Which film do you want to see?
